findings.title: Request fields evaluated as JavaScript
findings.evidence: `eval(req.body.preTax)`, `eval(req.body.afterTax)`, `eval(req.body.roth)` evaluate request fields as code.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user reaches remote code execution in the web tier with a single form field.
findings.fix: Parse the three contribution fields with `Number.parseInt` and reject non-finite values before persisting.

findings.title: NoSQL `$where` built from a query parameter
findings.evidence: A `$where` clause is built by interpolating the unvalidated `threshold` query parameter.
findings.impact: The threshold parameter is evaluated server-side by the database, exposing every allocation row.
findings.fix: Replace the `$where` clause with a typed comparison document and coerce `threshold` to a number.

findings.title: Unescaped user name written to the log
findings.evidence: The raw user name from the login form is written to the log, allowing CRLF log forging.
findings.impact: CRLF in the login form forges log lines, which defeats the audit trail an incident depends on.
findings.fix: Log through the structured logger and pass the user name as a field rather than string concatenation.

findings.title: Password persisted without hashing
findings.snippet:
// const hash = bcrypt.hashSync(password, salt);
user.password = password;
findings.evidence: The password is stored as received; the bcrypt hashing is commented out.
findings.impact: A database disclosure hands over every password in clear text, including reused corporate credentials.
findings.fix: Restore the bcrypt hash on write and the comparison on read; migrate stored rows on next successful login.

findings.title: Login distinguishes unknown user from wrong password
findings.evidence: Distinct error messages for an unknown user name and a wrong password.
findings.impact: The two distinct messages turn the login form into a user-enumeration oracle.
findings.fix: Return one message for both branches and keep the timing of the two paths comparable.

findings.title: Password policy accepts a single character
findings.evidence: `PASS_RE = /^.{1,20}$/` accepts any one-character password.
findings.impact: One-character passwords survive registration, so credential stuffing needs no list.
findings.fix: Require at least twelve characters and check the candidate against a breached-password list.

findings.title: Session cookie without `httpOnly`, `secure` or `maxAge`
findings.evidence: The session cookie is configured without `httpOnly`, `secure` or `maxAge`, under the default cookie name.
findings.impact: The session cookie is readable from script and travels over plain HTTP under the default name.
findings.fix: Set `name`, `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite: "lax"` and an absolute `maxAge` on the session store.

findings.title: Template auto-escaping disabled application-wide
findings.evidence: `swig.setDefaults({ autoescape: false })` disables template output escaping application-wide.
findings.impact: Every rendered template becomes a stored cross-site scripting sink, including the profile page.
findings.fix: Remove the override, then mark the few intentionally raw fragments at their call sites.

findings.title: Allocations page trusts a user id from the URL
findings.evidence: The allocations page takes `userId` from the URL parameter instead of the session.
findings.impact: Changing one path segment reads another customer's allocations.
findings.fix: Take the user id from the session and return 404 when the path segment disagrees.

findings.title: Security headers disabled and `x-powered-by` left on
findings.evidence: `x-powered-by` stays enabled and every helmet middleware (frameguard, noCache, CSP, HSTS) is commented out.
findings.impact: No framing, transport or content-source protection reaches the browser, and the stack is advertised.
findings.fix: Enable helmet with a content-security policy, HSTS and frameguard, and disable `x-powered-by`.

findings.title: Identity documents stored in clear text
findings.evidence: SSN, date of birth and bank account are stored in clear text; the encryption branch is commented out.
findings.impact: Social security number, date of birth and bank account sit unencrypted, a direct GDPR Article 32 failure.
findings.fix: Restore field-level encryption with a managed key and re-encrypt existing rows in a migration.

findings.title: Application listens over plain HTTP
findings.evidence: The server listens over plain HTTP; the HTTPS server and its key material are commented out.
findings.impact: Credentials and session cookies cross the network unprotected.
findings.fix: Terminate TLS in front of the app and redirect port 80, or restore the HTTPS listener and its key material.

findings.title: Benefits routes miss the administrator guard
findings.evidence: `/benefits` GET and POST require only `isLoggedIn`; the `isAdmin` guard is commented out.
findings.impact: Any signed-in user reads and edits the benefits of every employee.
findings.fix: Re-attach `isAdmin` to both the GET and the POST route and cover the pair with a regression check.

findings.title: No cross-site request forgery protection on state changes
findings.evidence: `csurf` is required but never mounted; no form carries a token.
findings.impact: A third-party page can move funds on behalf of a signed-in user.
findings.fix: Enable the CSRF middleware, emit the token into every form, and set `sameSite` on the session cookie.

findings.title: Manifest pins components with published advisories
findings.evidence: Pinned or floating old versions: marked 0.3.5, swig ^1.4.2, mongodb ^2.1.18, bcrypt-nodejs 0.0.3, needle 2.2.4, express ^4.13.4.
findings.impact: Known advisories reach production through direct dependencies nobody has bumped.
findings.fix: Upgrade the flagged direct dependencies, regenerate the lockfile, and add an advisory check to the pipeline.

findings.title: Redirect target taken from the query string
findings.evidence: `/learn` redirects to `req.query.url` without validation.
findings.impact: The application lends its domain to a phishing landing page.
findings.fix: Accept a relative path from an allowlist and reject anything carrying a scheme or authority.

findings.title: Server fetches a user-supplied URL
findings.snippet:
const { url } = req.query;
http.get(url, response => response.pipe(res));
findings.evidence: `needle.get(req.query.url + req.query.symbol)` fetches a caller-controlled URL from the server.
findings.impact: The request reaches the cloud metadata endpoint and any internal service the host can see.
findings.fix: Resolve the host, refuse private and link-local ranges, and restrict the fetch to an allowlist.

findings.title: Catastrophic backtracking in profile validation
findings.evidence: `/([0-9]+)+\#/` validates the bank routing number with nested quantifiers.
findings.impact: One crafted profile field pins a worker thread and takes the process out of rotation.
findings.fix: Replace the nested quantifier with a bounded pattern and cap the validated field length.

findings.title: Session secret hard-coded in the committed config
findings.evidence: The literal is present at the reviewed revision and is shared by every deployment reading this file.
findings.impact: Anyone with repository access can forge a session cookie for any user.
findings.fix: Read the secret from the environment at boot and fail closed when it is absent.

findings.title: Database credentials committed for the development profile
findings.evidence: The URI carries an inline user and password, and the same file is read when NODE_ENV is unset.
findings.impact: A production host booted without NODE_ENV uses development credentials.
findings.fix: Move the URI to an environment variable and refuse to boot on the development profile outside development.

findings.title: Transitive advisory reachable through the template engine
findings.evidence: The engine is unmaintained; its advisory is reachable from every rendered route.
findings.impact: No upstream fix exists, so the advisory stays open for as long as the engine is used.
findings.fix: Migrate rendering to a maintained engine and delete the dependency.

findings.title: Lockfile drifted from the manifest
findings.evidence: Three manifest ranges admit versions the committed lockfile does not pin.
findings.impact: A clean install resolves versions nobody reviewed.
findings.fix: Regenerate the lockfile in the same commit as any manifest change and gate it in the pipeline.

findings.title: No rate limit on the authentication routes
findings.evidence: Neither the route nor the server composes a limiter; every attempt reaches the password comparison.
findings.impact: Credential stuffing runs at network speed against a weak password policy.
findings.fix: Add a per-address and per-account limiter with exponential backoff in front of the login route.

findings.title: Stack traces rendered to the browser
findings.evidence: The development error handler is mounted unconditionally.
findings.impact: Internal paths and library versions reach any visitor who triggers an exception.
findings.fix: Mount the verbose handler only under the development profile and log the trace server-side otherwise.

findings.title: Profile updates logged with their payload
findings.evidence: The serialized document includes the bank account and the date of birth.
findings.impact: Personal data lands in log storage that carries none of the database's access controls.
findings.fix: Log the document id only, and route any payload logging through the redaction profile.

findings.title: Download route joins a user-supplied file name
findings.evidence: No normalization sits between the query parameter and the join.
findings.impact: A traversal sequence reads any file the process can open.
findings.fix: Resolve the joined path and refuse anything outside the upload directory.

report.markdown:
# Rapport de sûreté du code — OWASP NodeGoat

> Données d'exemple. Ce rapport est rejoué depuis les fixtures livrées avec le Command Deck ; il n'a pas été produit par une exécution en direct.

## Résumé (français)

Six départements de la division Code Safety ont lu 34 fichiers de `OWASP NodeGoat` à la révision `c5cb68a` et ont placé **26 constats** sur les lignes qui les portent : 6 critiques, 10 élevés, 8 moyens et 2 faibles.

Les cinq constats critiques partagent une même cause : l'application fait confiance à l'entrée de la requête avant de l'exécuter, de la rendre ou de la stocker. `eval()` sur trois champs de formulaire donne l'exécution de code à tout utilisateur authentifié ; la clause `$where` construite par interpolation expose l'ensemble des allocations ; l'échappement des gabarits est désactivé pour toute l'application ; les mots de passe et les pièces d'identité sont conservés en clair.

Le certificat couvre cinq départements sur six. Le département Platform reste **partiel** : la surface conteneur n'a pas pu être lue à cette révision, et deux constats de ce département sont marqués non vérifiés. Aucune remédiation n'a été appliquée : le périmètre de cette revue est la lecture, pas l'écriture.

### Recommandation

Traiter les 6 constats critiques avant toute mise en production, puis les 10 constats élevés dans la même itération, car le stockage des mots de passe et la protection de session se corrigent ensemble.

## Summary (English)

Six departments of the Code Safety division read 34 files of `OWASP NodeGoat` at revision `c5cb68a` and placed **26 findings** on the lines that carry them: 6 critical, 10 high, 8 medium and 2 low.

The five critical findings share one cause: the application trusts request input before executing, rendering or storing it. `eval()` over three form fields hands remote code execution to any authenticated user; an interpolated `$where` clause exposes every allocation row; template escaping is disabled application-wide; passwords and identity documents are kept in clear text.

The certificate covers five departments of six. Platform remains **partial** — the container surface could not be read at this revision, and two of its findings are recorded as unverified. No remediation was applied: the scope of this review is reading, not writing.

### Departments

| Department | Findings | Certificate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Secrets | 2 | certified |
| Injection | 5 | certified |
| Access | 7 | certified |
| Data | 4 | certified |
| Dependencies | 3 | certified |
| Platform | 5 | partial — container surface unread |

### Severity ladder

| Severity | Count |
| --- | --- |
| critical | 6 |
| high | 10 |
| medium | 8 |
| low | 2 |

### Provenance

Every ground-truth entry comes from `data/code-safety/targets/nodegoat.ground-truth.json`, read at revision `c5cb68a7084e4ae7dcc60e6a98768720a81841e8` of [OWASP NodeGoat](https://github.com/OWASP/NodeGoat). Findings whose id starts with `CS-` are departmental output beyond that ground truth and carry the lower confidence to match.
